# Keys and security

Source: <https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/keys-and-security>

Your partner portal's Administrators create your API keys. Each works in one environment, does only what its scopes allow and, in live, works only from the addresses you register.

## API keys

| Key | Starts with | Works on | Works from |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sandbox | `mgw_test_` | The sandbox host only | Any address, if it has no addresses. With addresses, only from them |
| Live | `mgw_live_` | The live host only | Only the IP addresses and ranges registered for it |

After the prefix, a key has 43 characters generated from 32 random bytes. Send it in the `Authorization` header as `Bearer` and the key. A key sent to the wrong environment's host returns `401 unauthorized`, with a message that says so.

### How keys are created

An Administrator creates keys on the API keys page of your partner portal, choosing the key's scopes and, for a live key, the IP addresses it works from. A key is for the environment you create it in, sandbox or live. The portal asks the Administrator to verify their identity again before it creates or rotates a key. There's no API to create a key.

The portal shows the key once. We store only a hash of it, so neither the portal nor we can show it again or recover it. If you lose a key, create a new one and revoke the old one. Keep keys on your servers, in a secrets manager, and never in an app or web page your customers download.

The portal creates a key, or rotates one with an overlap, only while your company holds fewer than 10 working keys. Revoked and expired keys don't count. A rotation with no overlap adds no key, so it's never refused for this. If no one at your company can sign in to the partner portal, [ask us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support) for a key. We send it once, through a [one-time link](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#how-keys-and-secrets-reach-you) to your technical contact.

A key works until it's revoked, or until the overlap after a rotation ends.

### Scopes

A key can do what its scopes allow. Choose them when you create the key.

| Scope | Lets the key |
|---|---|
| `read` | Make any `GET` request: accounts, orders, events, applications, the wallet, allocations and reference lists. |
| `trade` | Place, estimate and cancel orders. |
| `fund` | Make allocations from your wallet. |
| `apply` | Send account applications and their documents. |

Give each of your services a key with only the scopes it needs. A reporting service needs `read` alone. A key that tries something outside its scopes gets `403 insufficient_scope`, with a message that names the scope it lacks, and nothing is done. A rotated key has the same scopes as the key it replaces. We record when each key was last used, to the minute, so we can tell you whether a key is still in use before we retire it.

### Rotate a key

Rotate a key in your partner portal. The new key has the same IP addresses and scopes, and the portal shows it once. The old key keeps working for an overlap you choose, up to 7 days, then expires.

1. Rotate the key, with an overlap long enough to switch your servers.
2. Switch your servers to the new key within the overlap.
3. Revoke the old key once you've switched, or let it expire.

An expired key returns `401 unauthorized`, the same response as a revoked or unknown key. A rotation with an overlap needs room for one more working key. With no overlap, the old key stops as the new one starts, so it adds no key and is always allowed.

### Revoke a key

A revoked key stops working on its next request. Revoke a key in your partner portal. If a key leaks, revoke it at once: in the portal, or yourself with `POST /v1/keys/revoke`, sending the key in the `Authorization` header. Any key can revoke itself, whatever its scopes, and from any address, even one a live key isn't registered for. Then create a new key. Don't rotate a leaked key: rotation keeps it working through the overlap. See [If a key leaks](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#if-a-key-leaks).

Hold a second live key in reserve, for the same addresses and scopes, so revoking one never stops your trading.

### Live keys and IP addresses

A live key works only from the addresses registered with it: each address or range your servers send requests from, given when the key is created. A key's addresses are fixed then, so new addresses mean a new key: create one with them, switch your servers to it, then revoke the old one. Each entry is a single address, such as `203.0.113.10`, or a range, such as `203.0.113.0/29`. These two examples are documentation addresses, which a live key refuses: use your servers' own.

| Rule | Why |
|---|---|
| At least one entry. | A live key accepted from any address can trade for anyone who obtains it. |
| IPv4 ranges no wider than `/20`, and IPv6 ranges no wider than `/56`. | A wider range covers far more of the internet than your servers. |
| No private, loopback, link-local, multicast or unspecified addresses. | Requests from your servers reach us from public addresses. One of these would mean something between us hides the real sender, or would accept requests from any address. |
| No address, and no range touching a block, that the IANA special-purpose address registries mark not globally reachable, such as shared address space (`100.64.0.0/10`), documentation, benchmarking or reserved addresses. | The internet doesn't route requests from these, so no server of yours sends from one. |

We read the address from the connection itself, never from a header such as `X-Forwarded-For`. A request from an address that isn't registered returns `401 unauthorized`, the same response as an invalid key, so the response never confirms to someone holding a stolen key that it's valid. If your live requests start failing with `401`, check whether your servers' outbound addresses have changed.

## Connections

The API is served over HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or later. Over TLS 1.2 we negotiate only these cipher suites:

| Cipher suite |
|---|
| `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` |
| `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` |
| `TLS_ECDHE_ECDSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` |
| `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_128_GCM_SHA256` |
| `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_AES_256_GCM_SHA384` |
| `TLS_ECDHE_RSA_WITH_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256` |

A host negotiates the three that match its certificate's key, ECDSA or RSA. The sandbox's certificate is ECDSA. If your client limits its cipher suites, allow all six, so a new certificate never stops your connection.

The sandbox is HTTPS only, like live: a request to `http://` and the host gets no response and times out.

Our responses carry these headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `x-request-id` | An ID we create for the request, starting with `req_`. Log it, and include it when you [contact us](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/support#report-a-problem). |
| `Cache-Control` | `no-store`, so no cache keeps a response. |
| `X-Content-Type-Options` | `nosniff`, so a browser never reads a response as anything but its `Content-Type`. |
| `Content-Security-Policy` | `frame-ancestors 'none'`, so no page can frame a response. |
| `Strict-Transport-Security` | `max-age=63072000` on every response, sandbox and live, so a client that honours it uses HTTPS for the next two years. It covers the API host only. |

## Your customers' data

When you apply for an account, we pass your customer's identity details to the broker and don't keep them. For an application we store only:

- its state, the reason for it, and the field at fault if the broker named one,
- the broker's reference for it,
- the account number, once the account opens,
- your `client_reference` and `Idempotency-Key`,
- a keyed hash of the application, so we can tell a retry from a different application. The key for that hash isn't stored with our data,
- for each document you send, its type, its size, whether it's a JPEG or a PNG, what the broker said of it, and a keyed hash of the file, so we can tell the same file sent again. We never keep the file.

We never store or log a customer's name, date of birth, BVN, NIN, phone number, email address, home address, next of kin or bank details. An error names the field at fault in `param` and never repeats its value.

Balances, positions, trades and contract notes are read from the broker each time you ask, and we don't store them. We do store your orders, allocations and wallet ledger, and a record of each message we exchange with the broker about them. These carry account codes but no names. We also store your payout account's bank details, which your partner portal shows by their last four digits, and a note of each call we made to confirm them: whom we called, on which number, and when. Our logs record the route a request used, not its path, so account codes in a path aren't logged.

## Webhooks

Every event we send is signed. Verify each one before you act on it. See [Webhooks](https://docs.matambaintelligence.com/webhooks).
